stem: Albuterol is used to prevent and treat which cluster of respiratory symptoms?

options.label: A
options.text: Barking cough and stridor in viral croup
options.misconception: Treats all noisy breathing as bronchospasm, missing that stridor reflects upper-airway narrowing.
options.explanation: Croup narrows the subglottic upper airway; it is treated with corticosteroids and nebulized epinephrine, not albuterol bronchodilation.

options.label: B
options.text: Sneezing and nasal congestion in allergic rhinitis
options.misconception: Assumes an inhaled asthma drug also relieves nasal allergy symptoms.
options.explanation: Allergic rhinitis is an upper-airway condition treated with intranasal corticosteroids and antihistamines, not an inhaled beta-2 agonist.

options.label: C
options.text: Wheezing and chest tightness in asthma or COPD
options.misconception: None — albuterol relieves bronchospasm symptoms in asthma and COPD.
options.explanation: MedlinePlus lists albuterol to prevent and treat wheezing, breathlessness, cough and chest tightness caused by asthma and COPD.

options.label: D
options.text: Pleuritic chest pain and hemoptysis in pulmonary embolism
options.misconception: Assumes any acute dyspnea with chest pain responds to a bronchodilator.
options.explanation: Pleuritic pain and hemoptysis from pulmonary embolism reflect a clot in the pulmonary arteries, which is treated with anticoagulation.

options.label: E
options.text: Fever and productive cough in bacterial pneumonia
options.misconception: Confuses relief of airway narrowing with treatment of a lung infection.
options.explanation: Fever and productive cough from bacterial pneumonia need antibiotics; a bronchodilator does not treat the infection.

context: Learning objective: Albuterol is used to prevent and treat wheezing, breathlessness, cough and chest tightness caused by asthma and COPD.
